html:
The Oresteia is a trilogy of tragedies by Aeschylus, first staged in Athens in 458 BCE. It is the only complete trilogy of Greek tragedy that survives.

  • Agamemnon: the king comes home from the Trojan War and is murdered by his wife Clytemnestra.
  • The Libation Bearers: their son Orestes kills his mother to avenge his father.
  • The Eumenides: the Furies hunt Orestes until the goddess Athena sets up a court of citizens on the Areopagus to judge him. The votes are tied and Athena's vote sets him free.

The story turns an old chain of blood revenge into a story about law. Private vengeance gives way to a public trial, a fitting theme for the young Athenian democracy, which had cut back the powers of the Areopagus council only a few years before. The trilogy won first prize at the City Dionysia, the festival where tragedy had begun (first tragedy at the Dionysia). Aeschylus died two years later in Sicily. Sophocles and Euripides both wrote their own versions of Orestes and his sister Electra.
